newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - June 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - June 30.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

A Federal Government inter-departmental committee is drawing up a plan to make administrative tribunals financially dependant on the government departments they are supposed to keep in check. The tribunals would be placed under a new Commonwealth agency tat would have senior representatives from the bureaucracy.

The Industry Commission draft report released yesterday claims a move to cut textile, clothing and footwear tariffs to five per cent by 2008 would boost national income by around A$100 million a year. Tariffs on clothing are scheduled to drop to 25 per cet by the year 2000 while the rate on textiles and footwear is scheduled to come down to 15 per cent.

BHP is at a near-record market capitalisation of A$38 billion despite losing nearly A$7 billion over the past 15 years through poor investment decisions. As it announced more write-offs in its results for the year to May, it has made some good investmentdecisions such as the purchase of Utah's Australian coal interests. Page 1.
THE AUSTRALIAN

In response to an Australian Parliamentary report on the handover of Hong Kong, Beijing has warned Australia not to get involved in the affairs of the colony after 156 years of British rule ends at midnight tonight. The warning sent by the Chinese embassy in Canberra on instructions from Beijing coincided with Foreign Minister Alexander Downer's arrival in Hong Kong. Page 1.

Tasmanian poet Peter Shoobridge murdered his four daughters early yesterday, then posted suicide letters to family members, alerted authorities to a murder-suicide, then chopped off his right hand before shooting himself in the head. The murder took place at Shoobridge's home near Richmond, 20 kilometres east of Hobart. Page 1.

Darwin barrister and former Federal Labor backbencher John Reeves is expected to head the Howard Government's planned review of the controversial land rights laws which allow Aborigines to veto mining and other development projects on the 42 per cent of te Northern Territory they now own. Page 3.

The fatal shooting of a knife-wielding man by two New South Wales police officers on Bondi Beach early Saturday morning has reinforced calls by officers to be issued with mace or pepper sprays to disable offenders. New South Wales Police Association presient Phil Tunchon said firearms were the only immediate response available to police in high risk situations. Page 3.

On the eve of the deregulation of Australia's telecommunications industry, Communications Minister Richard Alston has predicted the traditional STD phone call may be replaced by cheaper State-wide charges. Alston says consumers will benefit from lower chrges in all areas of telecommunications. Page 3.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Australia has refused to join Britain in condemning China's move to deploy 4000 armed troops and armoured vehicles in Hong Kong just hours after the official handover from colonial rule at midnight tonight. Foreign Minister Alexander Downer also refused t join Britain and the United States in boycotting the swearing-in ceremony of the Beijing-appointed Provisional Legislature. Page 1.

The Productivity Commission's draft report on the textile, clothing and footwear industries to be released today recommends the Federal Government slash protection for Australia's struggling TCF industries to 5 per cent by 2008, two years ahead of the APE 2010 deadline, despite warnings from the industry that most of the 96,000 jobs in the industry would disappear. Page 1.

The Administrative Review Tribunal and four specialist review bodies are set to be axed by Federal Cabinet and replaced them with a government-controlled body, stripping citizens of their right to an independent review of the merits of Government decision against them. The plan has drawn strong protests from the Law Council of Australia. Page 1.

Immigration Minister Philip Ruddock says the Government would consider any appeal on behalf of British radiologist Dr Duncan Walker, who has been ordered out of Australia because his baby daughter has cerebral palsy. The Immigration Department refused Dr Walker's application for permanent residence because his two-year-old daughter could be a drain on taxpayers. Page 2. --
THE AGE

Foreign Minister Alexander Downer yesterday defended China's decision to send 4000 People's Liberation Army troops into Hong Kong at dawn on Tuesday, saying the transfer of sovereignty meant China was responsible for the defence of Hong Kong. Page 1.

The future of much of Australia's textile, clothing and footwear industry is in doubt after the industry Commission proposed slashing tariff protection to 5 per cent by 2008, and abolishing its two other support schemes - the import credit scheme and the y-law scheme. Page 1.

Prime Minister John Howard said Australia and the United States were sharing economic circumstances not seen for decades and said he believed Australians could be optimistic about employment prospects based on economic assessments from US President Bill Cinton and Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan. Page A2.

In a speech to the Tasmanian Gay and Lesbian Rights Group's dinner to celebrate the decriminalisation of homosexuality by the Tasmanian Parliament, High Court judge Justice Michael Kirby said Australian society was weak because of its dependence of leaving social reform to the courts. Page A3.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
